name: Maxillomandibular advancement (MMA)

angle.text: MMA moves both jaws forward and is marketed online as a looks-plus-airway upgrade, with the forward movement visible in profile. It is an established sleep-apnoea operation; its cosmetic use is studied less.

summary: Surgery that moves both jaws forward, established as a sleep-apnoea operation and marketed online as a looks-plus-airway upgrade.
note: The strong evidence is for sleep apnoea, not appearance; lower-facial numbness is very common early on and hardware removal is reported in a fifth of patients.
currentQuick:
Maxillomandibular advancement (MMA) is jaw surgery in which the upper and lower jaws are both cut and moved forward, enlarging the space behind the tongue and soft palate. It was developed within orthognathic surgery and is now one of the most studied surgical treatments for obstructive sleep apnoea, usually considered after other treatments such as CPAP or other sleep surgery have not worked.
In looksmaxxing communities, MMA and bimax are discussed as a way to advance the face and sometimes to fix breathing at the same time, with threads about rotation, midface expansion and surgeon choice. Sleep-apnoea outcomes are well documented in meta-analyses; evidence on cosmetic outcomes is much thinner.
How it works: A Le Fort I osteotomy frees the upper jaw and a mandibular osteotomy, typically a sagittal split, frees the lower jaw; both are advanced and fixed with plates and screws. Advancing the skeleton also pulls forward the soft tissues attached to it, widening the airway at the palate and tongue base.
Risks and caveats: A 2025 meta-analysis found early lower-facial numbness in about 83 percent of patients, persisting beyond a year in about a third, and hardware removal in about 22 percent. Other documented concerns include bleeding, airway swelling after surgery, relapse, jaw-joint problems and a longer recovery than other sleep surgeries.
deepLead:
Maxillomandibular advancement (MMA), also called bimaxillary advancement or Bi-Max, is a jaw operation that moves both the upper jaw and the lower jaw forward. It originated in orthognathic surgery for facial skeletal deformity and bite problems and was later applied to obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA), where it is classed as a type of sleep surgery.
For sleep apnoea, MMA is described in reviews as one of the most effective surgical options and a gold-standard surgical choice for refractory disease. A 2025 meta-analysis of 31 studies and 1,597 patients reported a mean fall in apnoea-hypopnoea index of about 42 events per hour, alongside high rates of lower-facial numbness and of hardware removal. The procedure is typically considered after other treatments have failed and requires a longer recovery than other sleep surgeries because the facial bones must heal.
In looksmaxxing communities, MMA is mentioned as a surgery that may combine facial advancement with an airway benefit, and users discuss how it interacts with other procedures such as maxillary expansion. Research on its cosmetic effects is limited compared with its sleep-apnoea literature.

name: Jaw surgery (orthognathic)

angle.text: Orthognathic surgery repositions the upper jaw, lower jaw and chin, and forum users treat it as the major structural option for a recessed jaw, facial balance and a straighter bite and smile. The change in jaw position is itself the visible result; reports note that functional gains and cosmetic outcomes do not always match.

summary: Corrective jaw surgery that repositions the upper jaw, lower jaw and chin for bite, airway and facial-balance goals; a legitimate surgical field that forums treat as the big structural lever.
note: Strong evidence is for bite, airway and function; cosmetic-only outcomes are less studied, and numbness, relapse and joint problems are documented.
currentQuick:
Orthognathic surgery is the medical term for jaw surgery that corrects the position of the upper jaw, lower jaw, chin or all three. It is used for underbites, overbites, open bites, asymmetry, jaw-joint problems and obstructive sleep apnoea, and it is also used to change facial proportions.
Looksmaxxing forums call it a hardmaxx procedure and discuss bimax, Le Fort I, genioplasty and related operations, with frequent questions about braces, insurance, recovery and complications. Medical literature documents functional outcomes and technique well, and is more limited on purely cosmetic goals.
How it works: Surgeons cut the jawbones from inside the mouth, move them to a planned position and fix them with titanium plates and screws, usually after orthodontic preparation. Virtual 3D planning, custom splints and patient-specific plates are increasingly used to transfer the plan to the operating room.
Risks and caveats: Reviews describe bleeding, swelling, infection, nerve numbness, jaw-joint effects, relapse, hardware problems and a recovery of weeks to months. A systematic review also estimated that body dysmorphic disorder is more common among orthognathic surgery patients than in the general community.
deepLead:
Orthognathic surgery, also called corrective jaw surgery, reshapes the jaws and lower face to treat structural, growth, airway, jaw-joint and bite problems, and can also be used for facial balance and symmetry. The operation is usually done through the mouth: bone is cut, moved and fixed in a new position, and it is typically coordinated with orthodontic treatment.
Main procedures include the Le Fort I osteotomy for the upper jaw, the bilateral sagittal split osteotomy for the lower jaw, and genioplasty for the chin; surgeons may combine them in two-jaw (bimaxillary) surgery. Reviews describe expanding indications for upper-airway obstruction, computer-assisted planning, patient-specific fixation and shifts in the orthodontic-surgical sequence over the past two decades.
In looksmaxxing communities it is treated as one of the most consequential procedures, discussed alongside implants, rhinoplasty and orthodontics, with extensive talk about risk and surgeon choice.

name: Chin implant / genioplasty

angle.text: Chin implants and sliding genioplasty add or reposition chin projection to balance the profile, with the change visible after healing. Both are routine surgeries, and forums describe bone sliding as the larger change.

summary: Two ways to build out the chin, a placed implant or a cut-and-slid piece of the jawbone; routine cosmetic and orthognathic surgery with the larger changes coming from bone.
note: Fixes chin position, not the bite; numbness, implant shifting or bone changes and asymmetry are documented risks.
currentQuick:
Chin augmentation changes the underlying structure of the chin to balance the rest of the face. The two main surgical approaches are an implant placed over the bone and a sliding genioplasty, in which a section of the lower jawbone is cut and moved forward, back, up or down. It is often done alongside a nose operation or jaw surgery.
On looksmaxxing forums the chin is a frequent target, with threads comparing genioplasty with bimax, asking how many millimetres are needed and discussing recovery and removal. Published reviews cover techniques, materials, stability and complications; there is little head-to-head research on which approach produces the best appearance.
How it works: An implant adds volume to the front of the chin through an incision inside the lip or under the chin. A sliding genioplasty cuts a horseshoe-shaped piece of bone from the lower edge of the jaw, repositions it and fixes it with plates and screws, so the tissue attached to it moves too.
Risks and caveats: Reported problems include swelling, hematoma, temporary lip or chin numbness, infection, implant displacement or bone changes under implants, nerve injury and asymmetry. Surgery is performed by plastic, facial plastic or oral and maxillofacial surgeons as regulated cosmetic or orthognathic surgery.
deepLead:
Chin augmentation, also called mentoplasty or genioplasty, changes the underlying structure of the chin to balance the rest of the face; it can add projection with an implant, reduce or round the chin through bone cutting, or change its height. Sliding genioplasty uses an osteotomy of the chin bone, while implants are placed in a pocket over the bone, usually through an incision inside the mouth or under the chin.
Reviews describe genioplasty as frequently done alone or with rhinoplasty, facelifts and orthognathic surgery and as an important element of lower-face aesthetics. A bone-based correction is described as usually giving a more dramatic result than an implant, while implants are the simpler operation. Neither approach corrects the bite.
On looksmax.org, chin surgery is discussed as a way to improve the profile, with threads asking how much advancement to seek and whether genioplasty alone is enough.

name: Jaw implants

angle.text: Jaw implants are used to widen and define the lower jaw, a visible change used in facial gender surgery and cosmetic work. Reviews note that more outcome research is needed.

summary: Implants placed along the angle and body of the lower jaw to widen or define it; used in facial gender surgery and cosmetic work, with little outcome research behind the forum hype.
note: Published outcome research is limited; users and reviews raise questions about design, size and how natural the result looks.
currentQuick:
Jaw implants, sometimes called mandibular angle or gonial implants, are solid shapes of silicone, porous polyethylene or PEEK placed over the lower jawbone to add width or definition at the angle and body of the jaw. In published literature they appear mainly in facial gender-affirming surgery, where augmentation of the mandibular angle and body is described as a masculinising option.
In looksmaxxing communities they are discussed as an alternative to bimax and genioplasty, with arguments about implant design, size, body fat and how natural the result looks. Outcome research on cosmetic jaw implants is thin.
How it works: An implant is placed against the bone through an incision, usually inside the mouth, and sits under the soft tissue so that the lower face contour looks wider or squarer. Some designs are custom-made from CT scans.
Risks and caveats: Reported concerns include a bloated or unnatural look when implants are too large or the underlying structure is mismatched, soft-tissue sagging after removal, infection and displacement, though complications are described as minimal in one gender-affirming surgery review. Outcome data are limited.
deepLead:
Jaw implants are alloplastic (manufactured) implants placed over the angle and body of the mandible to increase width and definition; they are also called mandibular angle or gonial angle implants. A review of lower jaw contouring in facial gender-affirming surgery describes augmentation of the mandibular angle, body and chin with alloplastic implants, fat or bone as a masculinising option and reports that complications are minimal, while stating that more research on outcomes is needed.
Few studies examine cosmetic jaw implants specifically. A retrospective CT study of cosmetic surgery foreign bodies in the maxillofacial region documented the imaging appearance of such materials as incidental findings, without describing implant outcomes.
On looksmax.org, jaw implants are debated as an alternative or complement to bone surgery such as bimax, with questions on sizing, leanness and whether the underlying structure suits an implant.

name: Cheek implants

angle.text: Cheek implants add fullness or projection over the cheekbone, and the new contour is visible after healing. Reviews report high satisfaction, but trial-grade evidence is limited.

summary: Solid silicone or polyethylene implants over the cheekbone for more projection; reviews report high satisfaction but a few percent to ~10% complication rates, and little trial-grade evidence.
note: Implant-related infection, displacement and visible prominence are documented; results depend heavily on implant shape and placement.
currentQuick:
Cheek implants are solid synthetic shapes, usually silicone or porous polyethylene, placed through the mouth onto or under the cheekbone to make the midface more projected or fuller. They are used for flat cheekbones, asymmetry, ageing and facial feminisation, and are discussed on looksmaxxing forums as a way to get higher cheekbones.
Reviews of the surgical literature report high patient satisfaction and low complication rates, but the evidence is mostly retrospective series. Forum users debate malar versus submalar shapes and custom versus stock implants.
How it works: An implant is positioned over the malar bone (malar), below it (submalar) or both, and fixed with sutures or screws, adding volume and projection that is permanent unless the implant is removed.
Risks and caveats: A 2025 meta-analysis of 3,701 patients found a 7.4% complication rate for malar implants (10.7% across facial implants), with heterogeneity. Reported issues include infection, displacement, visible prominence and asymmetry. Implants are Rx surgical devices placed by a surgeon under anesthesia.
deepLead:
Cheek implants, also called malar or submalar implants, are solid alloplastic (synthetic) devices placed over or beneath the cheekbone to increase midface projection or fullness. They are used to correct congenital cheekbone underdevelopment, asymmetry and age-related volume loss, and in gender-affirming facial surgery, and they are discussed in looksmaxxing communities as a way to obtain higher or more angular cheekbones.
The usual materials are silicone and porous high-density polyethylene (sold as Medpor), with expanded PTFE also used. The implant is typically inserted through an incision inside the mouth and stabilised with sutures or screws. Reviews describe the result as permanent but reversible, since the implant can be removed.
Published evidence consists mainly of reviews and case series rather than randomised trials. A 2025 meta-analysis of 48 studies reported an overall complication rate of 10.7% for facial skeletal implants and 7.4% for malar implants specifically, with substantial heterogeneity between studies. A 2018 systematic review found that malar implants had a high incidence of prominence problems. A 2008 review noted that enthusiasm for cheek implants appeared to be declining in favour of soft-tissue approaches such as fat and fillers.

name: Buccal fat removal

angle.text: Buccal fat removal is sought for a slimmer, more sculpted lower midface, a permanent change visible after swelling settles. Reviews report a 25% pooled complication rate, and no randomised trials exist.

summary: Intraoral removal of the cheek's buccal fat pad for a slimmer, hollower look; permanent, with a 25% pooled postoperative complication rate and no randomised trials.
note: Irreversible; facial nerve and parotid duct injury are reported, and a gaunt look with ageing is discussed.
currentQuick:
Buccal fat removal takes out part of the deep fat pad in each cheek through a small cut inside the mouth, aiming for a slimmer lower face and more visible cheekbone contour. It became widely discussed on social media in the early 2020s and is a common hardmaxxing topic on looksmaxxing forums.
Published evidence is mostly case series, a small single-arm trial and systematic reviews. Surgeons describe it as generally safe with careful anatomy, while forum users share both satisfied and botched outcomes.
How it works: The encapsulated pad is extracted by blunt dissection and suction through an intraoral incision, permanently reducing cheek volume. Because the pad is not lost with general weight loss, proponents say removal changes contour where dieting does not.
Risks and caveats: A 2025 meta-analysis of 308 patients reported 25% prevalence of postoperative complications, mainly swelling, trismus, pain and asymmetry, with rare facial nerve paralysis, infection or hematoma. Parotid duct injury is reported. The effect is permanent and may look gaunt with ageing, according to encyclopedia summaries.
deepLead:
Buccal fat removal, also called bichectomy or buccal fat pad extraction, is a cosmetic operation that takes out part of the buccal fat pad (Bichat's fat pad), a deep encapsulated pad of fat in each cheek, to slim the lower midface and create a more contoured or hollow-cheeked look. It is usually done through a small incision inside the mouth.
Looksmaxxing communities discuss it as a hardmaxxing option for people who stay round-faced even when lean. Surgical reviews describe it as generally safe with careful anatomical technique, but the evidence is mainly case series and small single-arm studies, and the fat pad does not regrow after removal.
A 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis of 12 studies and 308 patients reported an overall postoperative complication prevalence of 25%, mostly swelling, trismus and pain, with high heterogeneity between studies; serious events such as facial nerve paralysis, infection and hematoma were rare in that analysis. Wikipedia notes that removal carries a risk of damage to the buccal branch of the facial nerve and to the parotid duct.

name: Lateral canthoplasty

angle.text: Lateral canthoplasty is used medically for lid laxity and is now sought by people who want a more upward-tilted outer eye corner, which is a visible change. No studies test it for that cosmetic goal.

summary: Surgery on the outer eye corner, used medically for lid laxity and increasingly sought to raise canthal tilt; no studies test it for that cosmetic aim.
note: Cosmetic tilt change is untested; lid malposition risk is documented and DIY versions circulate online.
currentQuick:
Lateral canthoplasty reshapes or tightens the outer corner of the eye by working on the lateral canthal tendon. Surgeons use it to support a loose lower eyelid, for ectropion, and alongside lower blepharoplasty.
In looksmaxxing forums people ask about it for a more positive canthal tilt or a more almond eye. The published literature covers lid support, not cosmetic tilt, and forum users debate canthoplasty versus the gentler canthopexy.
How it works: The lateral canthal tendon is repositioned or tightened and anchored to the orbital rim, lifting and supporting the outer lid. Canthopexy uses sutures without detaching the tendon.
Risks and caveats: Reviews note that small changes can substantially alter lower eyelid shape and that malposition, round-eye deformity and ectropion are risks. Cosmetic canthal-tilt outcomes have not been studied, and self-performed versions discussed online have no published support.
deepLead:
Lateral canthoplasty is eyelid surgery that repositions or tightens the lateral canthus, the outer corner of the eye where the upper and lower lids meet. In ophthalmic and plastic surgery it is used mainly to support or tighten a lax lower eyelid, to prevent or correct lid malposition after lower blepharoplasty, and in facial palsy and ectropion repair.
In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed for a different aim: raising the outer corner to produce a more positive canthal tilt, a more almond or 'hunter' eye shape, or more visible sclera. Published surgical literature describes canthal procedures as supportive or functional, and no published study found here evaluates canthoplasty specifically for increasing canthal tilt in people with normal eyelid tone.
Surgeons distinguish canthoplasty, which involves cutting and reattaching the lateral canthal tendon, from the more conservative canthopexy, which supports the lid with sutures without detaching the tendon. Reviews note that small adjustments in this area can produce large changes in lower eyelid shape, and that excessive tightening or midface elevation can lead to round-eye deformity or ectropion.

name: Hunter eyes surgery

angle.text: Hunter eyes surgery is community slang for combined procedures meant to produce a deep-set, positively tilted eye look, visible after healing. No study tests that specific goal.

summary: Slang for combined eye-corner surgery (canthopexy, fat grafts, blepharoplasty) aimed at a deep-set, positively tilted look; no study tests that goal.
note: Not a standard named procedure; lid malposition and asymmetry are documented risks of the component surgeries.
currentQuick:
Hunter eyes surgery is looksmaxxing shorthand for operations meant to give a deep-set, positively tilted, low-lid-show eye look. In practice it usually means canthopexy or canthoplasty, sometimes combined with fat grafting or blepharoplasty.
The surgical literature studies these procedures for lid support and rejuvenation, not for creating this look, so the aesthetic goal itself has no direct trial evidence.
How it works: Canthal procedures reposition or suspend the outer lower eyelid and lateral canthus; fat grafting adds volume under the eye or brow; blepharoplasty reshapes lid tissue. Together they aim to change tilt and lid exposure.
Risks and caveats: Reviews describe lid malposition, scleral show, ectropion and shape changes as risks, noting that small changes around the canthus can have large effects. Results as a combined cosmetic package are only documented in forum posts.
deepLead:
'Hunter eyes' is looksmaxxing slang for an eye appearance usually described as deep-set, with little upper eyelid show, a low brow-to-lid distance, and a neutral or positive canthal tilt. 'Hunter eyes surgery' is the community term for surgical combinations intended to produce that look, most often canthopexy or canthoplasty at the outer eye corner, sometimes combined with fat grafting, brow or blepharoplasty procedures.
There is no single standard operation by that name in the surgical literature. The components are established procedures with other indications: canthopexy and canthoplasty for lower-lid support, lower blepharoplasty, and fat transfer to the periorbital region. Published studies assess these for lid position, rejuvenation and functional outcomes; no study located evaluates them as a package to create a 'hunter' look.
Canthopexy supports the lower eyelid, typically in conjunction with lower blepharoplasty to reduce the risk of lid malposition, and reviews describe it as the most conservative form of canthal suspension. Because small changes around the lateral canthus can change eyelid shape substantially, reviews call for caution in this area.

name: Orbital decompression

angle.text: Orbital decompression is discussed as a way to get deeper-set eyes, with the eye position change visible after surgery. Its established use is thyroid eye disease; cosmetic deep-setting has no trials.

summary: Orbital bone or fat removal that lets the eye sit deeper; a thyroid-eye-disease operation with no trials for cosmetic deep-setting.
note: Orbital surgery with risks to vision and eye movement; evidence comes from thyroid eye disease, not cosmetic use.
currentQuick:
Orbital decompression enlarges the eye socket by removing bone, fat or both so the eye sits further back. It is an established operation for thyroid eye disease, where swollen tissue pushes the eyes forward or threatens the optic nerve.
Looksmaxxing forums discuss it as a way to get deeper-set eyes without thyroid disease and debate candidacy and technique. No published trial studies it for that cosmetic purpose.
How it works: Surgeons remove parts of orbital walls (medial, lateral, floor) and/or orbital fat via endoscopic, conjunctival or other approaches, giving swollen or prominent contents room to move backward.
Risks and caveats: Reported complications in thyroid eye disease include optic neuropathy, corneal exposure, persistent double vision and raised eye pressure, and vision loss after decompression has been described in case reports. Forum posters call it among the riskiest hardmaxxing procedures.
deepLead:
Orbital decompression is surgery that enlarges the effective volume of the eye socket by removing orbital bone, orbital fat, or both, allowing the eye to sit further back. Its established use is in thyroid eye disease (Graves' orbitopathy), where swollen muscle and fat push the eye forward (proptosis) and can compress the optic nerve.
In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a way for people without thyroid disease to get deeper-set eyes by reducing protrusion, and members debate who is a candidate, which technique (fat removal or bone work) is used, and its risks.
The clinical literature on orbital decompression concerns people with thyroid eye disease. Randomised trials and case series compare surgical approaches and report outcomes such as proptosis reduction and sight-threatening optic neuropathy. No published trial located assesses the procedure for purely cosmetic deep-setting in people with normal thyroid and orbital status, and the surgery is an operation in the orbit with documented risks to vision and eye movement.

name: Blepharoplasty

chain: Excess lid skin and fat removed
angle.text: Blepharoplasty is used to reduce hooding and under-eye bags, with the result visible once swelling settles. It is established for those concerns; looksmaxxing-specific eye-shape goals have no trials.

summary: Eyelid surgery to remove or reposition excess skin and fat; established for hooding and bags, with no trials for looksmaxxing-specific eye-shape goals.
note: Dry eye and lower-lid malposition are documented risks; fat preservation is increasingly emphasised.
currentQuick:
Blepharoplasty is the standard operation for droopy upper lids and lower-lid bags, removing or repositioning skin, muscle and fat. Surgeons also perform it to improve vision when lids obstruct sight, and East Asian double-eyelid surgery is one of the most common variants.
Looksmaxxing members discuss it for eye shape, ptosis and tiredness, usually combined with fat grafts or brow work. Surgical literature supports it for dermatochalasis and bags; claims about dramatic eye-shape changes are mainly forum accounts.
How it works: Incisions in the lid crease (upper) or beneath the lashes or inside the lid (lower) allow removal, repositioning or preservation of skin, muscle and fat. Canthal support may be added to stabilise the lower lid.
Risks and caveats: Swelling and bruising are common for weeks; dry eye, lid malposition and asymmetry are reported complications, and a 1987 infection cluster was traced to contaminated skin-marking solution. Surgeons often combine it with canthal support to reduce malposition.
deepLead:
Blepharoplasty, commonly called eyelid surgery, is plastic surgery that removes or repositions excess skin, muscle and fat of the upper or lower eyelids. It is performed for functional reasons, such as heavy upper lids that reduce peripheral vision, and for cosmetic reasons, such as reducing hooding or under-eye bags.
In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a hardmaxxing option for the eye area, often alongside fat grafting, brow repositioning or canthal procedures, and members debate whether it would improve eye shape, ptosis, or perceived tiredness.
Reviews describe upper blepharoplasty as having both aesthetic and functional outcomes, and a 2023 systematic review compared techniques and outcomes including effects on the cornea, intraocular pressure, dry eye and visual quality. A 2026 review characterised modern practice as having shifted from subtractive techniques toward tissue preservation and augmentation. Wikipedia notes the procedure is more common in women (about 85% of US cases in 2014) and that Asian (double-eyelid) blepharoplasty is among the most common procedures in several East Asian countries.

name: Brow lift / brow bone augmentation

chain: Younger or more masculine upper face
angle.text: Users pursue brow lifts to raise a low or tired-looking brow, and brow bone augmentation for a stronger, more masculine ridge; the change in brow position or shape is visible right after healing. Brow lifting is established for brow ptosis, while bone augmentation for appearance is documented mostly in reconstructive and gender-affirming work.

summary: Surgical or injectable ways to raise the eyebrows or reshape the brow ridge; established for brow ptosis, while bone augmentation for a stronger brow has little published evidence outside reconstructive and gender-affirming work.
note: Surgical brow lifts are established procedures with rare but real complications; reviews describe all techniques as limited in longevity.
currentQuick:
A brow lift raises a low or drooping eyebrow and can smooth forehead lines. Techniques range from botulinum toxin and fillers to endoscopic, temporal and direct surgical lifts. In looksmaxxing communities it is often listed alongside other hardmaxxing procedures, because brow position and brow ridge projection are discussed as part of the eye area.
Brow bone augmentation or reduction reshapes the bony ridge above the eyes using implants, grafts, cement or burring. The published literature on this sits mostly within craniofacial and gender-affirming surgery rather than appearance enhancement in general, and no trials were found testing it for looksmaxxing goals.
How it works: Surgical lifts release and reposition the forehead and brow soft tissue, often by altering the depressor muscles and fixing the brow higher; endoscopic approaches use small scalp incisions. Botulinum toxin can raise the brow by weakening the muscles that pull it down. Bone augmentation adds material over the supraorbital ridge or frontal bone, while reduction removes or recontours bone.
Risks and caveats: Reviews describe complications of brow lifts including scalp numbness, hair loss at incisions, hairline change, asymmetry, infection and bleeding, with technique-specific differences, and note that no brow lift technique is considered completely satisfactory in longevity. Non-surgical options are temporary. Forum participants discuss surgery abroad and the risk of poor results.
deepLead:
A brow lift (also forehead lift, browplasty or browpexy) is a cosmetic or reconstructive procedure that raises a low or drooping eyebrow and may soften forehead lines . Techniques include endoscopic, coronal, direct, temporal, hairline and transblepharoplasty approaches, plus non-surgical options such as botulinum toxin and soft tissue fillers . A published review of ten popular techniques concluded that none is completely satisfactory because of limited effectiveness, longevity or complications .
In looksmaxxing and hardmaxxing discussion, brow lifts are listed within multi-procedure plans, for example alongside genioplasty, lip lift, canthoplasty and blepharoplasty, often performed abroad . Community posts also discuss brow bone implants and reducing frontal bossing, a separate group of procedures involving the skeleton rather than soft tissue. Published work on brow bone contouring is concentrated in facial feminization and masculinization surgery, where forehead reduction or augmentation is an established part of gender-affirming care.
Evidence for soft-tissue brow lifting consists mainly of surgical case series, narrative reviews and a limited number of small randomized trials; no trial has tested brow bone augmentation for appearance enhancement in people without gender-affirming or reconstructive indications.

name: Facial masculinization surgery

chain: Forehead, brow, jaw and chin reshaped
angle.text: Looksmaxxers borrow facial masculinization techniques such as forehead and brow work, jaw and chin augmentation, aiming for a squarer, more masculine face; the skeletal change is visible once healed. The literature is mostly reviews and case reports from gender-affirming surgery rather than studies of appearance goals in cisgender men.

summary: Gender-affirming craniofacial surgery that squares the jaw, projects the chin and builds up the forehead and brow; the literature is mostly reviews and case reports, and looksmaxxers borrow the techniques for appearance goals.
note: A major surgical category using implants, grafts and osteotomies; published evidence is largely reviews and case series.
currentQuick:
Facial masculinization surgery (FMS) is an umbrella term for procedures that make facial features read as more masculine, chiefly forehead and brow augmentation, jaw and chin augmentation, and Adam's apple enhancement. It is mainly performed as gender-affirming care for trans men and other transmasculine people.
In looksmaxxing circles the same toolkit is discussed for cis men who want a more prominent forehead, brow ridge or jaw. Forum posts ask how to change the forehead shape without work on the bone, and are often redirected in search results to facial feminization procedures such as brow bone shaving.
How it works: Surgeons add or reshape skeletal and soft tissue: forehead implants, bone grafts, bone cement or fat grafting; jaw angle and chin implants or osteotomies; and cartilage grafts at the thyroid cartilage. Planning often uses CT scans and virtual surgical planning with custom guides and implants.
Risks and caveats: Complications depend on the procedure and include infection, implant movement or asymmetry, and nerve injury in jaw and chin work. Published evidence for facial masculinization is mostly reviews, case reports and book chapters, and the field has received less research attention than facial feminization.
deepLead:
Facial masculinization surgery (FMS) is a group of reconstructive and aesthetic procedures that make facial features more masculine, mainly performed as gender-affirming surgery for trans men and transmasculine people . Procedures include forehead augmentation to create a less rounded forehead and stronger brow ridge, jaw and chin augmentation, and a rib-cartilage procedure to enlarge the Adam's apple first reported in 2017 .
Surgical planning commonly relies on CT scans compared with a reference skull, with custom cutting guides and implants . Wikipedia notes that FMS is less common than facial feminization surgery and that its literature is mostly case reports, reviews and book chapters . The Wikipedia article describes FMS as rarely medically indicated because testosterone often produces enough change in the facial skeleton, while a 2016 WPATH position statement considers it medically necessary for many trans men .
The term also appears in looksmaxxing discussion, where members consider skeletal forehead and jaw work for masculine appearance goals . No studies were found that examine FMS for cisgender appearance enhancement.

name: Hair transplant (FUE/FUT)

angle.text: Users get hair transplants to restore a hairline and add density where pattern hair loss has thinned the scalp, with grafted hair visible as it grows in. It is an established, durable procedure whose results depend on donor supply and surgeon skill; forum posters often discuss timing relative to ongoing loss.

summary: Surgical relocation of follicles from the back of the scalp to thinning or bald areas; an established, durable procedure that depends on donor supply and surgeon skill.
note: Transplanted hair does not stop native hair loss from continuing, and quality varies widely between clinics.
currentQuick:
A hair transplant moves hair follicles from a donor area, usually the back and sides of the scalp, into areas of thinning or baldness. The two main harvesting methods are follicular unit transplantation (FUT, or strip surgery) and follicular unit extraction (FUE), in which individual follicular units are taken with small punches.
Medical literature describes it as a well-established treatment for androgenetic alopecia and some other conditions, based on the principle of donor dominance. Looksmaxxing forums discuss it heavily, including trips to clinics in Turkey for lower prices, and members disagree about how reliable results are.
How it works: Hair follicles from the donor area are genetically resistant to the hormone-driven miniaturization of pattern baldness and tend to keep that behavior after relocation, which is called donor dominance. FUT removes a strip of scalp that is dissected into grafts; FUE removes units one at a time. Grafts are placed in tiny recipient sites, where they shed and regrow over months.
Risks and caveats: Reported effects include swelling, itching, temporary numbness, scarring at the donor area, temporary shedding of the transplanted hair, folliculitis and infection. Native hair around transplanted areas can continue to thin, so surgeons often combine surgery with medical therapy. Quality and safety vary by clinic, and forum posts describe poor outcomes as well as good ones.
deepLead:
Hair transplantation is a surgical procedure in which hair follicles from a donor region, typically the back and sides of the scalp, are relocated to areas of hair loss . It is used mainly for androgenetic alopecia (male and female pattern hair loss), and also for some scarring alopecias and to correct trauma or prior surgery . Modern practice is built on follicular unit transplantation, in which naturally occurring groups of one to four hairs are used as grafts .
The two main ways of obtaining grafts are follicular unit transplantation from a harvested strip (FUT, strip surgery) and follicular unit extraction (FUE), in which individual units are removed with small punches. FUE was described in a 2002 paper and has since been joined by robotic systems . A 2025 review concluded that both FUE and strip excision are state-of-the-art methods and that hair transplantation has grown in popularity because of advances in devices, techniques and medical therapies that maintain density .
Hair transplantation has become one of the most discussed procedures in looksmaxxing communities, including clinic tourism to Turkey, where Wikipedia reports prices as low as about 1 US dollar per graft compared with several times that in some Western countries . Forum members debate candidacy, hairline design and the reliability of advertised success rates .

name: Beard transplant

angle.text: Men with patchy or absent facial hair use beard transplants to fill the jaw and cheeks for a fuller beard, which becomes visible as grafts grow in. Evidence consists of surgeon-reported series described in hair restoration reviews rather than controlled trials.

summary: Follicular unit grafts moved to the jaw and cheeks to fill patchy or absent facial hair; described in surgical reviews as a refined procedure, with outcome data limited to surgeon-reported series.
note: Published evidence is surgeon-authored reviews and experience reports; no controlled trials were found.
currentQuick:
A beard transplant moves hair follicles, usually from the scalp, into areas of the face where beard growth is sparse or absent. It is a branch of hair restoration surgery and uses the same graft-based techniques as scalp transplantation, with small recipient sites angled to match natural beard direction.
Surgical reviews describe it as having grown in importance because of its natural-looking results. The available literature consists mainly of surgeon experience, such as one review reporting more than 700 primary beard transplants by a single author, rather than controlled studies.
How it works: Grafts containing one or two hairs are harvested, trimmed to a minimal cuff of skin and placed into tiny recipient sites using the smallest possible blades, with angulation and design chosen to look natural. Transplanted hair is expected to keep the traits of its donor area.
Risks and caveats: Reviews discuss reparative procedures for poor results, and general hair-transplant risks such as swelling, scarring and infection apply. A looksmaxxing-specific evidence base is absent; no forum material is cited here.
deepLead:
Beard transplantation is the surgical relocation of hair follicles, usually taken from the scalp, to areas of the face where facial hair is thin, patchy or absent. It sits within hair restoration surgery alongside eyebrow, sideburn and eyelash transplantation .
A 2024 review by a surgeon with experience of more than 700 primary beard transplants and many repair procedures states that restoring the beard area has become an important part of hair restoration surgery because of its natural-appearing results, and emphasizes careful graft dissection, acute angulation of recipient sites and aesthetic design . A 2013 review similarly describes beards, goatees and sideburns as popular procedures whose results can be outstanding .
The evidence consists of expert reviews and personal series. No controlled trials of beard transplantation were found.

name: Eyebrow transplant

angle.text: Users pursue eyebrow transplants to thicken sparse brows or reshape them, and some discuss it as a way to lower a high brow position. Small surgeon series report high satisfaction and the result is visible once the grafts grow in; no controlled trials exist.

summary: Hair grafts placed to build denser or reshaped eyebrows; small surgeon series report high satisfaction, with no controlled trials.
note: Evidence consists of surgeon-reported case series; matching hair curl and growth direction is described as critical.
currentQuick:
An eyebrow transplant relocates individual hair follicles into the brow, to add density, fill gaps or reshape the brow. Surgeons describe the brow as small but demanding, because angle, direction, density and hair curliness must match the natural pattern.
Published reports are case series with satisfaction surveys and few complications. On looksmax.org, members mention eyebrow transplants when planning appearance changes, such as thicker or longer brows, alongside other surgeries.
How it works: Follicular units are harvested, by follicular unit extraction, from the scalp or the area behind the ear and placed into small recipient sites angled to follow the brow. A long-hair extraction technique lets the surgeon see hair curl to match it. Periauricular (around-the-ear) hair has been used because it grows slowly and is fine, like brow hair.
Risks and caveats: Reported series describe few complications, but they are small and surgeon-authored. Mismatched curl, direction or density can produce unnatural results, and reviews describe corrective operations after unsatisfactory work.
deepLead:
Eyebrow transplantation is a hair restoration procedure in which follicular units are moved into the eyebrow to increase density, fill sparse areas or reshape the brow . Reviews describe it as having become popular, and follicular unit extraction (FUE) as the most popular technique .
A 2021 case series of 36 patients treated with the long hair follicular unit excision technique reported natural results and satisfaction, with patient and surgeon scores of 4.7 and 4.3 on a five-point scale; twelve patients had had unsatisfactory surgery elsewhere and four had touch-ups . A 2024 retrospective study of 81 patients used periauricular hair and reported no significant complications over 15 months of follow-up .
Evidence is limited to such case series and expert reviews. No controlled trials of eyebrow transplantation were found.

name: Facial fillers (jawline/chin/cheek)

chain: Filler adds volume at jaw, chin, cheek
angle.text: Users inject hyaluronic acid and similar fillers to sharpen the jaw angle, project the chin and raise the cheeks without surgery, with the contour change visible immediately. The approach is temporary and adjustable, and fillers are well studied overall, though less so for young-adult contouring specifically.

summary: Injectable hyaluronic acid or similar fillers used to add projection to the jaw, chin and cheeks without surgery; temporary and adjustable, with rare but serious vascular risks.
note: Vascular occlusion, though rare, can cause tissue necrosis or vision loss; results are temporary.
currentQuick:
Facial fillers are injectable gels, most commonly hyaluronic acid (HA), placed under the skin to add volume or projection. In appearance culture they are used for the jawline, chin and cheeks, sometimes under the name facial balancing, as a temporary and reversible alternative to implants.
A 2023 analysis of Google search trends found that interest in jawline filler among men rose more than almost any other cosmetic procedure from 2004 to 2021. Forum members describe filler as a way to test or approximate a stronger jaw before, or instead of, surgery.
How it works: The filler adds soft tissue volume and, for firmer products placed deeper, structural projection. HA fillers are valued because of immediate effect and the ability to be dissolved with an enzyme (hyaluronidase). Other fillers include calcium hydroxylapatite (CaHA) and poly-L-lactic acid (PLLA), the latter stimulating collagen over time.
Risks and caveats: Common effects include bruising, swelling, redness and lumps. Rare serious events include vascular occlusion with tissue necrosis, and in some regions vision loss; reviews describe the jawline and several other areas as high-risk and high-reward. Fillers are regulated as medical devices, and approvals vary by country and area treated.
deepLead:
Dermal fillers are injectable materials placed in the skin or deeper tissue to restore or add volume . For the jawline, chin and cheeks they are used to sharpen the jaw angle, project the chin and raise cheek contour, an approach sometimes called facial balancing . Hyaluronic acid (HA) is the most widely used filler material and is biodegradable; other materials include calcium hydroxylapatite and poly-L-lactic acid .
A 2026 review of high-risk, high-reward filler areas states that HA fillers offer immediate correction and reversibility and remain central to treatment of the temple, jawline, lip and nose, and that complications range from contour irregularities to tissue necrosis, vision loss and embolic events . The review says safer treatment depends on region-specific vascular anatomy, conservative volumes, slow injection and appropriate depth, and that cannulas may reduce vascular occlusion risk compared with needles .
Jawline filler has been rising in popularity among men: a 2023 Google Trends analysis of 19 procedures found jawline filler among those with the largest increases in interest between 2004 and 2021 . In looksmaxxing communities, members compare filler with jaw implants and share before-and-after posts .

name: Calcium hydroxylapatite filler (Radiesse)

chain: Firmer jaw, chin and cheek contour
angle.text: Radiesse is a dense filler that users choose for firmer jaw, chin and cheek structure, with forum posters comparing it to a bone-like effect. It gives immediate volume and is reported to stimulate collagen; trials have mostly involved ageing faces rather than young-adult contouring.

summary: A dense, collagen-stimulating injectable filler used for cheek, jaw and chin structure; studied mainly in ageing faces, with little trial data on young-adult contouring goals.
note: Nodules are the most commonly reported adverse event; vascular occlusion is a rare but documented risk of all fillers.
currentQuick:
Calcium hydroxylapatite (CaHA) filler, best known by the brand name Radiesse, is a gel containing tiny calcium-based microspheres. Clinicians inject it to add volume and structure to areas such as the cheeks, jawline and chin, and it is also described as stimulating the body's own collagen.
In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a firmer, 'high G prime' option for a more defined jaw or chin without surgery. Published research mostly concerns older patients rather than young people seeking facial definition.
How it works: The gel carrier gives immediate volume while the microspheres act as a scaffold. Reviews describe nearby cells responding by producing collagen, elastin and other tissue components, with the gel itself gradually absorbed.
Risks and caveats: A review of 21 studies covering 5,081 treatments reported adverse events in about 3 percent of treatments, almost all nodules [4]. Fillers as a category carry a rare but serious risk of vascular occlusion, including blindness [12]. In the US, fillers are regulated as medical devices that a provider must inject [19]; approved indications for Radiesse are limited, and many facial contouring uses are off-label [2].
deepLead:
Calcium hydroxylapatite filler, sold most prominently as Radiesse (Merz Aesthetics), is an injectable soft-tissue filler made of calcium hydroxylapatite microspheres suspended in a carboxymethylcellulose gel . It is classed as a biostimulatory filler because, besides giving immediate volume, it is reported to induce new collagen, elastin and blood vessel formation in the surrounding tissue .
Clinicians use it for wrinkles and folds, cheek and jawline contouring, facial lipoatrophy in people with HIV and hand rejuvenation; off-label uses include skin tightening with diluted or hyperdiluted preparations . In looksmaxxing communities it appears under the label 'high G prime filler', as a firmer non-surgical option for adding structure to the jaw, chin and cheekbones.
A 2024 systematic review concluded that CaHA/CMC may be considered a safe and effective option for the cheeks, jawline, HIV-related lipoatrophy and nasolabial folds, while noting that no randomized controlled trials had been published on diluted and hyperdiluted techniques . A review of the safety literature found nodules to be by far the most commonly reported adverse event .

name: Black-market / DIY fillers

chain: Self-injected into jaw, chin or lips
angle.text: Forum users discuss buying filler outside regulated channels and injecting it themselves as a low-cost way to add jaw, chin, cheek or lip structure. Filler itself is well studied when clinicians administer it; the self-injection practice rests on forum anecdote.

summary: Filler bought outside regulated channels and injected without a clinician; the practice exists on forums, and the main risks are those regulators and reviewers attach to all fillers, with no safeguards.
note: Vascular occlusion, including blindness and tissue death, is a documented complication of filler injection even in clinical settings.
currentQuick:
Black-market or DIY filler refers to dermal filler products that people obtain outside licensed medical channels and inject into their own faces. On looksmaxxing forums it is presented as a way to enhance the jaw, chin or lips without visiting a clinic.
The forum material consists of user guides and personal plans, not research. Published sources on dermal fillers describe the injection of fillers by trained providers; no studies of self-injection were identified.
How it works: Users describe injecting hyaluronic acid-type gels of different firmness to add structure or soften transitions in areas such as the jaw, chin and lips. Fillers in general work by adding volume at the injection site.
Risks and caveats: Reference sources describe bruising, redness and pain as common effects of dermal fillers, and rare but serious complications including blindness caused by material reaching the eye's arteries, usually permanent when it occurs [1]. In the US, fillers are regulated as devices that a provider must inject [1]. Forum posters themselves discuss vascular occlusion and nerve injury as risks.
deepLead:
Black-market or DIY filler is the practice of buying injectable dermal filler outside regulated medical supply and administering it to oneself, as described on looksmaxxing forums. It overlaps with the broader topic of unlicensed injection of fat-dissolving agents and botulinum toxin, which some users discuss in the same threads .
Reference sources state that in the United States dermal fillers are approved as medical devices and a provider must prescribe and perform the injection, while in the UK and EU they are non-prescription devices under a CE mark that does not itself require proof of efficacy . Wikipedia's overview lists bruising, redness and pain as common effects of fillers, infection and allergic reactions as less common, and blindness from retrograde embolization into the ophthalmic and retinal arteries as rare but typically permanent .
No published study of self-injected filler was identified. Material about the practice comes almost entirely from forum posts, which this article describes only in general terms.

name: Masseter Botox

chain: Slimmer lower face, softer jaw outline
angle.text: Looksmaxxers use masseter Botox to slim a wide or boxy lower face by reducing jaw muscle bulk, and it is also used for teeth grinding. It is reasonably studied for muscle prominence, results are temporary, and a 2025 trial is the main data on effects on the bone.

summary: Botulinum toxin injected into the jaw muscle to slim a wide lower face; reasonably studied for muscle prominence, but temporary, and a 2025 trial is the main data on bone effects.
note: Effects wear off and need repeat treatment; asymmetry and weaker chewing have been reported, and bone-density effects are still being studied.
currentQuick:
Masseter Botox is the injection of botulinum toxin type A into the masseter, the main chewing muscle at the angle of the jaw. The goal is to weaken the muscle so it shrinks over time, slimming a square or wide lower face. It is also used for teeth grinding and jaw pain.
Looksmaxxing forums discuss it both as a facial slimming option and as something that suits some skull shapes and not others. Several pharma-sponsored trials of onabotulinumtoxinA for masseter prominence have been registered, while use for appearance has been off-label.
How it works: Botulinum toxin blocks the release of acetylcholine at the nerve-muscle junction, which causes the injected muscle to weaken [18]. With less use, the masseter is reported to lose bulk over weeks [2].
Risks and caveats: Reviews describe adverse effects as minimal and short-lasting [2], while Wikipedia notes that injecting the masseter can reduce chewing ability and that spread of toxin can weaken unintended muscles [18]. Researchers have examined whether reduced chewing load changes jawbone density; one placebo-controlled trial found no clinically significant change [3], while a smaller retrospective radiograph study in bruxism patients found region-specific reductions in a bone texture measure [5].
deepLead:
Masseter Botox is the injection of botulinum toxin type A into the masseter muscle, the thick muscle that closes the jaw . It is used to treat masseter muscle hypertrophy or prominence, a benign enlargement that can widen the lower face, and to treat bruxism (teeth grinding) and jaw pain . In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a way to slim the lower face and soften a boxy jaw outline.
Reviews report that botulinum toxin injected into the lower back portion of the masseter decreases muscle bulk and reshapes the lower face, with improvements in clenching symptoms and adverse effects described as minimal and short-lasting . A 2022 review noted that there were no standard guidelines for the procedure . Several company-sponsored randomized trials of onabotulinumtoxinA for masseter prominence have been conducted .
Interest in the procedure is visible in search data: a Google Trends analysis of 20 cosmetic procedures reported that search interest in masseter Botox changed by more than 50 percent within single weeks, one of four terms that did .

name: Lip filler

angle.text: Users get hyaluronic acid lip filler to add volume, define the lip border and balance upper and lower lip. The change is visible straight away, is temporary, and is well documented in trials; some forum rating systems weigh mouth width more heavily than lip fullness.

summary: Injected gel that adds lip volume and definition; well documented in trials, temporary, and a minor lever in forum rating systems that put more weight on mouth width.
note: Swelling and bruising are common; vascular complications are rare but serious, and results fade as the filler is absorbed.
currentQuick:
Lip filler is the injection of a gel, most often hyaluronic acid (HA), into the lips to add volume, define the border or improve proportions. It is one of the most widely performed non-surgical cosmetic treatments, and multiple randomized trials have compared HA lip products.
In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a cheap, low-commitment tweak for thin lips, though some posters argue that mouth width matters more than fullness and that filler cannot widen the mouth.
How it works: HA gels bind water and add volume where injected, and reviews call HA the gold standard lip filler because it is biocompatible and reversible [2]. Other methods include fat transfer, collagen and permanent fillers, with different durations [17].
Risks and caveats: Swelling and bruising commonly last up to a week [17]. Reviewers of lip safety describe complications that can be severe, note that complications are underreported, and say prospective randomized trials on the safety literature are lacking [4]. Overfilling can look unnatural [17].
deepLead:
Lip filler, or lip augmentation with fillers, is the injection of a soft-tissue filler, most commonly a hyaluronic acid (HA) gel, to increase lip volume, enhance the vermilion border or improve the ratio between the upper and lower lip . Perioral tissues are among the first to show ageing, and reviews say many patients seek perioral fillers as their first cosmetic treatment .
Reviews describe HA fillers as the gold standard for lip augmentation because they are biocompatible and reversible . Randomized, multicenter trials have compared HA gels with each other, including a head-to-head comparison of four products . Fat transfer and surgical approaches such as the lip lift are alternative methods .
A review of lip-filler safety states that the results are impressive but so are the reported complications, that there is a paucity of prospective randomized trials on safety, and that complications are under-reported . In looksmaxxing communities lip filler is discussed as a small, accessible modification, alongside views that proportions of mouth to nose matter more than lip volume .
